what_success_looked_like_vs_what_happene.expected: Fix 3 named tests with mock_aws and a skip, then copy one workflow file to main. Two small, mechanical steps.
what_success_looked_like_vs_what_happene.happened: Both steps rested on false premises, and measurement caught both before either shipped. Step 1's three named tests were symptoms of one fixture in a fourth file; the prescribed fix would have hidden it. Step 2's one file would have been red on arrival and would have deleted an existing job. The gate is now green in CI on the branch (proven twice) and green against main's code on PR #222, and Step 4's silent-J4 hypothesis is falsified rather than inherited.
what_success_looked_like_vs_what_happene.the_pattern_worth_keeping: Three of this handoff's five steps contained a stated cause that measurement contradicted. In every case the instruction was specific enough to be checked, which is why the error was catchable. A vaguer handoff would have produced a green gate hiding the same bug.
